target_customer: Software teams and solo builders who build with AI coding agents
problem: Chat tools treat agents as second class and keep work and talk apart. Party is a shared workspace where teams and agents plan, build, review and ship in one thread with budgets, sandboxing and memory.
business_model: Freemium SaaS with credits: free, 20 dollar starter, 200 dollar pro, custom enterprise
product_category: Multiplayer AI agent workspace for software teams

founders.name: Christian DalSanto
founders.background_notes: Per his YC page bio. The page does not say whether Party grew out of Maitai.

technical_complexity.rationale: Multi user real time sessions with agent harnesses, bring your own keys and tenant sandboxing are solid engineering but not research.

defensibility.rationale: Coding agent tooling changes quickly and large players can ship collaboration features; no data or network lock in shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not found. The product site positions itself against Slack and Teams, and a YC request for startups in Fall 2026 lists a multiplayer AI workspace category.

market_need_then: In 2024 AI coding agents were spreading but team collaboration around them was weak; the founder's pitch is that comms first tools treat agents as second class. No quantified demand evidence found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Collaborative and playful, tagline Build in the open. Together.

branding.brand_signature: Party themed community events such as Multiplayer Hackathons and Build Nights in the Bay Area
branding.community_and_virality: Hosted Multiplayer Build Night and hackathons in San Francisco, the Peninsula and Redwood City per Luma listings. No merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly, memorable word that fits the multiplayer idea and supports event based community building, but extremely generic and hard to search; evidence of reach is limited to small events.

outcome_analysis: Party is active with a working product, public pricing and community events, but no public funding or traction numbers were found, so no clear success or failure story can be told. It competes in a fast moving area where chat platforms, coding agent vendors and other YC companies are building similar multiplayer agent workspaces.
notes: No funding information found in two searches, so coverage is none_found (unknown, not zero). The YC page lists Christian DalSanto as the only founder; a Party contact in event listings is named julian@party.build but no role is stated, so he is not listed as a founder. The competitor search about Maitai returned only 2026 vendor pages, so the list is empty. Education not found. No outcome events found.
